page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c2d server family. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25 percent, despite average raw memory bandwidth read and write speeds. In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations, while achieving strong text generation speeds during small-model LLM inference.

The c2d-highcpu-16 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated AMD EPYC processor cores provide predictable execution times. This hardware configuration is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference.
